newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes slide lower on late selling burst.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes slide lower on late selling burst.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices faltered Tuesday, ending on the down side as a result of nervous selling ahead of weekly inventory reports.

Before the American Petroleum Institute (API) report was released late Tuesday, forecasts called for a more than 1 million barrel build in distillate stocks due to warm weather in heating oil zones across the eastern U.S. at year's start.

Expectations were more than met, after the API reported a 2.94 million barrel build in the distillates. Crude stocks were off close to 9.5 million barrels and gasoline supplies up 4.26 million barrels. Refinery runs were steady at 92.3 pct.
February West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ended 15 cts lower at $26.20-30 a barrel. Feb/Mar WTI closed out at 70 cts.
Outright deals were confirmed in the domestic aftermarket for Feb WTI at $26.20, 3 cts weaker than the NYMEX settlement.
The U.N. announced approval for a trio of Iraqi crude contracts under the oil-for-food deal, raising the number of contracts okayed to 24 since the plan's start on Dec 10.

Iraqi oil exports were seen peaking at around 620,000 barrels per day (bpd) in the late February, early March period of the six month plan. Managing the deal has been made complicated by the strong interest shown by a large number of oil companies, and the ever-stronger world oil price.
Various contracts have been altered by Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) in order to trim volumes to avoid hitting the $2 billion ceiling for oil sales.
Trading sources said it was not Iraqi crude, but Russian Urals that may have put pressure on the West Texas Sour/Midland market Tuesday.
Trades as weak as a $1.48 discount to the WTI marker pushed the main sour grade down some 6-12 cts from levels confirmed on Monday, before it bounced back.
The talk of Urals coming to the U.S. could not be confirmed by the company said to be involved.
Other activity had Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James go off at a 31-34 cts premium to the WTI/Cushing, ending an interesting session for the key sweet grade.
"It was very active, starting out at 33 cts (over WTI/Cushing), then moving down to 25 cts. Pressure from alternative crudes and refinery maintenance were behind it," said a crude broker in Houston.
Brent barrels were heard bought for delivery to the U.S. Gulf, taking advantage of the wide WTI-Brent spread.
Feb WTI-Brent was at $1.65-75 and March around $1.55-60, extending a trend for wider arbitrage opportunities.
One domestic crude buyer said they continued to buy foreign barrels, and noted the downward path of the LLS may be a sure signal the market realizes the arb dynamic.
Still, major LLS players said the grade would likely find comfort around 40 cts over the marker by month's end, stronger than current prices but well below the 80 cts-$1.00 premium seen last year.
Other trades saw Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire sell at 16-18 cts over the WTI/Cushing, and Midland/WTI at 2-5 cts below the even level to WTI/Cushing.
